Reserved serial/USB flashing acceptance for audits 1768 and 1572

Generation is offline. Every case starts not_run. The Unix PTY fixture proves
real driver/lock/retry/callback boundaries, not USB enumeration, ESP reset lines,
ROM SLIP exchanges, flash durability or post-flash firmware compatibility.

Prepare the inventory JSON with host {os: linux|macos, identity, os_build, owner,
uid, reserved_account:true}, board {reserved:true, serial, hardware_id, owner,
model, recovery_instructions, catalog_board, chip, device_name, cp210x:{path,
vid_pid:10c4:ea60, usb_serial, location}, native:{path, vid_pid:303a:1001,
usb_serial, location}, native_replug_path}, cli_source_commit, cli_binary,
identity_record, recovery_record, blank_state_record, reinstall_state_record,
app_review_record, main_manifest, firmware_manifest, firmware_binary and project.
Run from the candidate checkout:
  python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/serial-flash-rehearsal.py INVENTORY.json NEW_OUTPUT
Inspect NEW_OUTPUT/evidence.json, commands.json and procedure.txt before any device
operation. Generation only hashes local records and seeds its new private cache.
The record paths contain existing owner-reviewed evidence, not generated claims.
Use an ESP32 development board with independently documented CP210x UART and
native USB Serial/JTAG connectors. The bridge's USB serial is not the ESP chip ID.
Record the physical board serial, ESP factory MAC/hardware ID, chip model, flash
size, bridge USB identity, connector labels and exact host USB topology together.
Run this matrix separately on each supported host OS/driver qualification being
claimed. This generator covers Unix hosts; Windows reset/driver acceptance stays
pending until the same matrix is separately run there.

The recovery record must contain the board vendor's exact boot/reset instructions,
validated prior firmware/config backup and an owner-operated restore command for
this board. Reserve an isolated bench board without production data, actuators,
attached serial peripherals or production credentials. Obtain erase authorization
for this exact fingerprint before either install or reinstall. A non-Wendy blank
baseline and a known incompatible Wendy Lite baseline must each have an immutable
image hash and reviewed preparation/restore instructions. Never infer blank state
from an unresponsive port alone. Do not execute a generic erase command on another
connected device. Disconnect all other install-capable ESP32/UART boards.

Use the CLI built from the recorded revision. Verify its hash before each phase.
Record current GCS master.json and its selected firmware manifest, plus the exact
published .bin checksum/size. Generation seeds only the new private cache with
these verified original bytes. The production interactive ESP installer selects
latest stable from the live manifest; --version and --binary do NOT pin a Lite
image, and --device-type rejects ESP32. There is no invented firmware-path flag.
Re-fetch and compare manifest selection immediately before each run, and retain
the printed Found firmware version, cache path and original cached SHA256 after
it. If selection or bytes differ, stop and regenerate the plan; do not count the
trial. The config partition is modified in memory by production provisioning.
Do not hash that resulting flash as if it were the unmodified release archive.

Run commands below in a real terminal as the recorded reserved UID, with terminal
transcript capture owned by that account. The guardian preserves the terminal and
bounds command descendants. Capture separate CLI return status and actual elapsed
time. Do not use --force, --yes, --json on interactive install/run, or pipe Yes.
Generated HOME/profile/cache are fresh and contain no Cloud login. Commands avoid
pre-enrollment; decline any optional Cloud prompt in the reinstall flow. Record
system USB inventory before and after each cable move, including changed tty path.
Do not open a competing serial monitor during CLI flashing. A passive logic trace
of DTR/RTS/EN/BOOT is useful only on a qualified electrically safe test connector.

1. CP210x first flash (1768). Restore the reviewed blank baseline, connect only
   CP210x, and run install. Select exactly the catalog board named at the end of
   this document. Confirm the candidate text says USB-UART, not a confirmed ESP
   model. With --no-wifi, explicitly accept the install-only warning only because
   the same board has the verified native connector. Require ROM identification
   to match the expected chip before any erase/write, complete flash and reset,
   and zero error exit within 900 seconds. CP210x staying enumerated across reset
   is expected; it must not appear as a WendyCom runtime device. Connect native
   USB on the same physical board, run discovery and identity_before. Require
   the recorded hardware ID, requested name and exact installed firmware version.
   A success banner or a CP210x tty alone does not pass post-boot identity.

2. Native first flash/reset (1768). Restore the same reviewed blank baseline,
   connect only native USB, record its identity, and run install for the same
   board. Require native reset/re-enumeration and complete ROM write/reset with
   the same identity/version afterward. Exercise one bootloader-entry retry with
   the owner-operated BOOT/RESET sequence from the recovery record; record the
   original failure, new port inventory and explicit reselection if its path
   changes. No unrelated candidate may be selected automatically. Record all
   attempts. Stop at the command deadline rather than killing another process.

3. Real disappear/reappear (1572). With the known firmware running, record the
   native port and successful identity. Run discover, disconnect the native cable,
   then run discover again after the OS removes the tty. No old serial entry may
   remain. Move to the prequalified different host port and require the recorded
   native_replug_path and the same physical USB/ESP identity; run identity_after.
   The new row must be responsive and carry the same board hardware identity.
   Separately repeat from the reviewed non-Wendy baseline: its opened but failed
   WendyCom handshake must appear as unflashed, then disappear on unplug. A busy
   port or a missing-node error must never be taken as proof of blank firmware.
   The automated PTY historical controls supply deterministic failure sensitivity;
   these physical observations qualify USB enumeration and real device behavior.

4. Reinstall/reconnect (1572). Restore the reviewed incompatible Wendy Lite image
   that actually lacks the harmless project's declared capability, not a fabricated
   CLI error. Project source/hash and required capability are in app_review_record.
   It must emit a unique trial heartbeat and never access motors/GPIO/other devices.
   Reconnect at the original native path and run reinstall. Require the actual
   capability error and destructive reinstall prompt, then explicitly approve this
   reserved board, select its catalog board and complete flash. Require production
   'Waiting for the device to restart', same-board identity, successful second
   build/deploy and new app heartbeat. Native recovery is bounded by production's
   5-second boot delay plus 30-second ready window; the whole build/install command
   is bounded at 900 seconds. A successful independent later command does not make
   a failed same-command reconnect pass. Record a changed-path reinstall separately;
   if it fails, preserve the failure and do not relabel fresh discovery as recovery.
   Run a decline trial first and verify original firmware/app remain intact. The
   CLI's --yes behavior is covered by existing units; it must not authorize erase.

5. Wrong-chip refusal (1768). On the same reserved blank board, choose a catalog
   target with a different ROM chip model. Require the expected-chip mismatch and
   nonzero exit before any FLASH_BEGIN/erase/write progress. Preserve the exact
   transcript and independent before/after baseline identity/flash evidence from
   the owner's read-only ROM tool. If absence of writes cannot be observed, retain
   this physical case pending; existing validation units alone are not that proof.
   Never run a historical wrong-chip bypass on hardware.

6. Restoration. Stop only the reviewed test app through its verified Lite lifecycle
   action or restore the exact reserved board firmware/config using the recorded
   recovery command. Power-cycle and re-read hardware/firmware identity. Join all
   owned CLI/monitor processes, reconnect original cables and restore recorded host
   port permissions if the owner changed any. Do not kill unrelated port holders,
   delete shared caches or log into production Cloud. Retain transcripts, original
   payload hashes, USB inventory, return statuses and recovery evidence under this
   private output directory; secrets must be removed before sharing. A failed
   restore means failed cleanup, not a completed hardware pass.
